59: // ClientFilterBuilder is an optional interface that a Builder can implement to
60: // indicate its capability to build client-side filters.
61: type ClientFilterBuilder interface {
62: 	// BuildClientFilter constructs a ClientFilter.
63: 	BuildClientFilter() ClientFilter
64: }
65: 
66: // ClientFilter represents the actual filter implementation on the client side.
67: // Implementations are free to maintain internal state when required, and share
68: // it across interceptors. Filter instances are retained by the resolver as long
69: // as they are present in the LDS configuration.
70: type ClientFilter interface {
71: 	// Close releases resources associated with the filter.
72: 	Close()
73: 
74: 	// BuildClientInterceptor uses the given FilterConfigs to produce an HTTP
75: 	// filter interceptor for clients. config will always be non-nil, but
76: 	// override may be nil if no override config exists for the filter.
77: 	//
78: 	// It is valid for this method to return a nil Interceptor and a nil error.
79: 	// In this case, the RPC will not be intercepted by this filter.
80: 	//
81: 	// The returned cleanup function is to be invoked when the interceptor is no
82: 	// longer needed.
83: 	BuildClientInterceptor(config, override FilterConfig) (interceptor iresolver.ClientInterceptor, cleanup func(), err error)
84: }

86: // ServerFilterBuilder is an optional interface that a Builder can implement to
87: // indicate its capability to build server-side filters.
88: type ServerFilterBuilder interface {
89: 	// BuildServerFilter constructs a ServerFilter. The returned cleanup function
90: 	// is to be invoked when the filter is no longer needed.
91: 	BuildServerFilter() (filter ServerFilter, cleanup func())
92: }
